notes.title: Post-Mortem
notes.content:
[h2][b]Lootfest for Steam – Post-Mortem[/b][/h2][p]Lootfest is a failed Early Access project that I regret — a big, ugly stain on my developer career. So what went wrong?[/p][p][/p][p][b]**Burnout**[/b][/p][p] By the time I got the Steam license, the project had already been in development for seven years, and all I could see were the bugs and issues.[/p][p][/p][p][b]**Massive Technical Debt**[/b][/p][p] Lootfest was my learning project — my first fully 3D game, my first networked game, my first menu system, etc. Lootfest 2 became an impossible knot of broken beginner code, which made me want to start over from scratch.[/p][p][/p][p][b]**Minecraft Clone Obsession**[/b][/p][p] At the time, there was a huge surge in Minecraft clones, and I felt Lootfest was seen as just another one. As the issue grew, I kept changing the art direction in an effort to look unique.[/p][p][/p][p][b]**Unhealthy Lifestyle**[/b][/p][p] When I got the Steam license, it still felt like a ticket to guaranteed success. But as Steam opened up to more and more developers, the pressure to work every hour of every day grew unbearable.[/p][p]

[b]**Being a Bad Boss**[/b][/p][p] I invested a lot of my own money to hire someone for a year. I thought giving him complete creative freedom would inspire great work, but it just led to experimentation with a lot of fun features — few of which were ever completed.[/p][p][/p][p][b]**No Soul**[/b][/p][p] Stripping out all the wild randomness, as well as the resource collection and crafting, removed what made the game fun in the first place.[/p][p][/p][p][b]**Handmade Content**[/b][/p][p]Lootfest started as a “Zelda forever” project — the idea was that if I randomized everything, it could be played forever, right?[/p][p]But as I removed the randomness, I had no idea how much work it would take to handcraft all the levels. I remember working on a dungeon with a boss for two months, and when it was complete I ran through the level and killed the boss in two minutes - thinking “I’m screwed!”.[/p][p][/p][p][b]**Wrong Platform**[/b][/p][p] In the end, Lootfest was a console game for kids and simply not suited for the Steam audience. I also underestimated how different PC development is. I wasn’t alone — just look at other major XBLIG games like Total Miner; we all struggled to adapt.
[/p][p][i]*I will remove Lootfest from Steam in about a month.*[/i][/p]

notes.title: Lootfest HD remake
notes.content:
[img]https://i.imgur.com/DyetCJi.png[/img]

I remade the art style of the game. The blocks are now 6 times smaller and has a flat color instead of a texture. I was going for a 16bit pixel art style - in 3D.

The current version has a creative mode only, which I will work on for a while before I add monsters and levels again.

Each block uses a 16bit value that combines 4096 different colors with 15 material types. I am not currently using the materials, but they will used to set properties to the blocks - like making breakable glass and such.

The game got 216 times more blocks and 432 times the amount of data. I broke the memory limit of XNA and had to port the game to MonoGame.

You can access the old adventure version by selecting it from the list of Betas:
[img]https://i.imgur.com/t471yoB.jpg[/img]

notes.title: Lootfest is a failure
notes.content:
I've now been working on Lootfest for 8 years! The complexity of the game has grown and is now far too big, specially for a single person project.
It is clear to me now that the game will never become what I initially planned.

[b]What mistakes has been made:[/b]
[list]
    [*]Early access doesn't work for me. I get almost no feedback, people don't report bugs/crashes. People expect a almost complete game and just get a negative experience. My end goal has always been to make people happy, and this is the opposite.
    [*]I started planning a full 16 hour experience. Should have started much smaller.
    [*]By streamlining the game, removing crafting and collecting, I killed what many enjoyed about the original game.
    [*]I thought more persons would play with a controller. It is too much of a console game.
    [*]The person I hired did not work out, had to throw away most of the code, mainly for the level layout and start over from scratch.
[/list] 

[b]What will happen now:[/b]
I will continue working on the game, but not at full time, it will be a side project.
I am thinking about making some big changes. For one I want to make a big change to the art style, and try move away from "just another Minecraft clone" as much as possible.
I will not leave early access until I am happy with the result. I am thinking about hiding the store page until it is a full release, haven't decided yet.
I will at least change the game description to warn about these issues.

I will answer any questions you got in the comments below.

notes.title: Big changes - long time to next update
notes.content:
[img]http://i.imgur.com/XU22d3e.jpg[/img]

[img]http://i.imgur.com/cRylmZT.jpg[/img]

[b]Cuts in development costs[/b]
In short I've had a few unlucky losses of income, and had to cut down on development costs. I could no longer afford having Martin on the team (We are still good friends and all) . I also had to leave the office I rented, and moved development back home again.
The development will go on, but at a bit slower pace.

[b]No updates for a long time[/b]
Martin was working on a system that created levels, but when working on the next update (see images) I started to realize it was too complicated and buggy for me to figure out. 
I will create a new level system that is easier to use and debug. But that will probably take me the whole summer, and you wont see any updates until that is done, sorry.

[b]Price cut[/b]
I initially planned to have about 20 hours of content for 15$, but because a few bumps on the road it is clear that the game will land at about 4-6 hours. The price is too high for that, I will lower it to 1$ for early access and 3$ at release.
I plan to update the game for another two years after release.

notes.title: Update: Online Multiplayer & Support for all Controllers
notes.content:
Big new year update is here!
[b]*Online Multiplayer.[/b] Is still in an early stage, expect many bugs!
[b]*Supporting any controller[/b] (including Steam Controller)
[b]*Rebindable keys.[/b]
[b]*Skybox.[/b] 
[b]*Hats![/b] The amount of appearance options has been doubled.
[b]*All monsters are in the card game.[/b]
[b]*Spawn director.[/b] The random monster spawn has been replaced by an overall manager that tries to keep the difficulty at an even level. It still bugs out sometimes and spawns a hundred monsters in one spot - working on that.
[b]*New level layout.[/b] It's now easier for us to make better levels, did not find the time to make one as example - of course.
[b]*Cinematic camera system.[/b] Being used when you travel.

[img]http://i.imgur.com/ETXMD7w.png[/img]
[i]The skybox was inspired by Destiny (you can see stars). There are hidden secrets in the sky ;) [/i]

[img]http://i.imgur.com/JcVxG9T.jpg[/img]

notes.title: Modify any model
notes.content:
Example of replacing the weapon and eyes
[url=http://imgur.com/ipgQyly][img]http://i.imgur.com/ipgQyly.jpg[/img][/url]

You can replace any model in the game (like monsters and weapons models).
1. Save a model in the Voxel Editor.
2. Go to “...Documents/My Game/Lootfest/VoxelObjSave” to find your save file.
3. Rename the file to the model you want to replace. For example the start weapon is named "stick", your heroes eyes are "Eye_Normal" and the pigs are named "Pig". To find out what the file is named, go to "Load">"In Game"> And you get a list of all models in the game.
4. Move the file to the "ReplaceModels" folder.
5. Start the game and enjoy!

-The collision boxes will still be like the old ones, for example a sword doesnt hit more just because you make it bigger.
-Some characters are a combination of models, like the hero is a combination of "Character", "hair_normal", "EyeNormal", "MouthSmile" and "belt_slim".
-Some models use color replacement, like the color on the heroes clothes. The replacement colors are:
*clothes/main color: rgb red
*pants/sub color1: rgb green
*shoes/sub color2: rgb cyan
*hair: rgb blue

-This info can also be found in the manual
